intro: Week 7 took out two of the league's three best records. Seattle beat Kansas City and Atlanta beat San Francisco, which leaves Minnesota alone at 6-0. Cowboys at Eagles closes the week tonight. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Chiefs and 49ers both lose, Vikings are the last unbeaten team
top.dek: Seattle beat Kansas City 20-3 on Sunday night. The Chiefs never reached the red zone and Harrison Butker missed from 58 and 45 yards. Atlanta also knocked off San Francisco 29-20, and Minnesota is now the only team without a loss at 6-0.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Lamar Jackson sits with a high ankle sprain, Week 8 return expected
top.dek: The Ravens ruled Jackson out Saturday, and he has now missed three games counting the second half of Week 4. NFL Network reported he was close to playing and is expected back against Buffalo on Sunday. Tyler Huntley threw for 298 yards in a 35-13 loss to Cincinnati.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Matthew Stafford passes Roman Gabriel as the Rams' touchdown leader
top.dek: Stafford threw three touchdown passes in a 35-21 win over the Raiders, two to Davis Allen and one to Puka Nacua. He now has 155 as a Ram. He finished 23 of 29 for 195 yards.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 540: Aaron Rodgers' career touchdown passes
top.dek: Rodgers hit Darnell Washington on a 77-yard, six-play drive for his 540th. That moved him past Peyton Manning into third on the all-time list. Pittsburgh beat New Orleans 16-10 in Paris.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Panthers visit Packers on Thursday night
top.dek: Carolina is at Lambeau Field on Thursday, Oct. 29 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. The Panthers lost right tackle Taylor Moton to a fractured fibula and gave up 258 rushing yards in a 43-13 loss to Tampa Bay. Green Bay comes off a 20-17 loss in Detroit.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills rest at 5-1 as Ravens loom

stories.text: Bills hit the bye at 5-1 with Ravens up next
stories.summary: Buffalo beat the Raiders 33-30 in Week 6 and used Week 7 to rest. The Bills host Baltimore on Nov. 1, and CBS Sports reporter Tracy Wolfson says Lamar Jackson is confident he will be back from his ankle injury for that game. Buffalo's pass defense has struggled this season, so a healthy Jackson would test it.

stories.text: Moore and Oliver expected back, Gardner-Johnson out
stories.summary: Coach Joe Brady said the hope is that receiver DJ Moore (AC joint sprain) and Ed Oliver (knee) return after the bye, and that he likes to think they are close. Moore played four games before the bye and Oliver three. Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson drew a one-game suspension for spitting at a Raiders player. If it stands, he misses the Ravens game.

stories.text: Josh Allen ties Jim Kelly with a backhanded flip
stories.summary: Allen went 23 of 33 for 255 yards and two touchdowns without an interception in Las Vegas. His 12-yard touchdown pass to Keon Coleman tied Jim Kelly's franchise record of 258 career touchdown passes, postseason included. Coleman finished with four catches for 59 yards.

stories.text: 258: Allen now shares the Bills record for TD passes
stories.summary: Allen's touchdown to Coleman against the Raiders put him level with Jim Kelly at 258 career touchdown passes, counting the playoffs. CBS Sports called the backhanded flip a possible play of the year. Allen's next touchdown pass sets the franchise mark.

stories.text: Sunday, Nov. 1: Ravens at Buffalo, 1:00 PM ET, CBS
stories.summary: The Bills return from the bye at home against Baltimore. Watch whether Lamar Jackson plays after missing Week 7 with an ankle injury, and whether Moore and Oliver are back on the field. Buffalo won the last meeting on a last-second field goal after trailing 40-25 in the fourth quarter.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Dolphins finally win, Hafley gets No. 1

stories.text: Dolphins beat Jets 28-25 for Hafley's first win
stories.summary: Miami held off a late Jets rally at MetLife Stadium for its first win of the season and the first for coach Jeff Hafley. The Dolphins led 21-7 at halftime and led most of the way. Malik Willis made the 2-yard push on fourth-and-1 that closed it out.

stories.text: Wright out with quad injury, two others hurt
stories.summary: Running back Jaylen Wright left in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. Safety Dante Trader Jr. hurt his left shoulder in the third quarter. Cornerback JuJu Brents left with a stinger but came back in the fourth quarter. De'Von Achane was lost earlier this season, so Wright's status matters for the backfield.

stories.text: Malik Willis finds Caleb Douglas twice, runs for one
stories.summary: Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns, both to rookie Caleb Douglas. He also ran eight times for 37 yards and scored on a 2-yard scramble before halftime. Douglas's second touchdown, a 63-yard catch and run, put Miami up 28-17.

stories.text: 103: Ollie Gordon II's rushing yards fill the Achane void
stories.summary: Gordon ran 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown with Achane out. Miami's 28 points were a season high. The Dolphins ran for 156 yards as a team on 41 carries, which kept the ball away from Geno Smith for most of the afternoon.

stories.text: Sunday, Nov. 1: Patriots at Miami, 4:25 PM ET, CBS
stories.summary: Miami hosts New England in Week 8 after its first win. Watch the run game with Wright's quad injury in question, and whether Willis keeps pushing the ball to Douglas against a Patriots team coming off a loss in Chicago.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots fall 30-24 in Chicago

stories.text: Patriots lose 30-24 to Bears on Thursday night
stories.summary: New England trailed 27-14 early in the second half and pulled within three, but Kyler Gordon sacked Drake Maye on fourth-and-5 to turn the ball over on downs. Cairo Santos then hit a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left, and Chicago recovered the onside kick after Andy Borregales cut it to 30-24. The Patriots fell to 4-3.

stories.text: Doubs and Vera-Tucker both land on injured reserve
stories.summary: Receiver Romeo Doubs hurt his shoulder against the Jets and goes on injured reserve for at least four games. Coach Mike Vrabel set no timeline and said the team will have to work without him for a while. Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker was also placed on injured reserve on Oct. 22, and the Patriots elevated Xavier Newman-Johnson and Benton Whitley from the practice squad.

stories.text: Drake Maye throws for 321 in the loss
stories.summary: Maye went 24 of 31 for 321 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, and ran in a 7-yard score. His 30-yard touchdown pass to Eli Raridon cut the Bears' lead to 27-21. D'Marco Jackson picked him off in the end zone earlier.

stories.text: 321: Maye's passing yards in Chicago
stories.summary: Maye threw for 321 yards on 24 of 31 passing with a 117.8 passer rating, but the Patriots ran 17 times for only 70 yards. The offense moved the ball through the air and still lost by six.

stories.text: Sunday, Nov. 1: Patriots at Dolphins, 4:25 PM ET, CBS
stories.summary: New England travels to Miami for a Week 8 game against a Dolphins team that just won for the first time this season. Watch how the Patriots line up on an offensive line without Vera-Tucker and a receiver group without Doubs.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets lose to winless Dolphins, 2-5

stories.text: Jets blow it against a Dolphins team seeking win No. 1
stories.summary: New York lost 28-25 at home to a Miami team that had not won all season, and coach Aaron Glenn's seat is a story now. The Jets never led, and the run defense has allowed 304 rushing yards over two weeks. Garrett Wilson was targeted three times and was seen in a sideline exchange with Geno Smith, which Wilson called collaboration.

stories.text: Hall and Parham still out, Sweat hurts knee
stories.summary: Running back Breece Hall and Dylan Parham stayed out another week even though both returned to practice. Defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat left late in the second quarter with a knee injury and did not return. Adonai Mitchell came back from a finger injury.

stories.text: Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. posts a second straight 100-yard game
stories.summary: Cooper caught five passes for 115 yards and a touchdown. He became the first Jets receiver with 100 yards in back-to-back games since Al Toon in 1985. Braelon Allen added 104 yards on 17 carries.

stories.text: 304: rushing yards the Jets allowed in two weeks
stories.summary: The run defense gave up 304 combined rushing yards over the last two games, and Miami held the ball for nearly 35 minutes on Sunday. Missed tackles and penalties added to the damage. Miami ran for 156 yards on 41 carries.

stories.text: Sunday, Nov. 1: Raiders at Jets, 1:00 PM ET, Fox
stories.summary: The Jets host Las Vegas in Week 8 looking to avoid a third straight loss. Watch whether Hall returns, how Sweat's knee holds up, and whether Wilson gets more than three targets.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens blow 13-0 lead, lose to Cincinnati

stories.text: Ravens give away a halftime lead and fall to the Bengals 35-13
stories.summary: Baltimore led 13-0 at the half at home and then watched Cincinnati score 35 straight. The Ravens are 4-3 and have lost two in a row. Tyler Huntley made his third straight start with Lamar Jackson out.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson's ankle: out Sunday, expected back for Buffalo
stories.summary: The Ravens ruled Jackson out for Week 7 on Saturday with what The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec reported is a high ankle sprain. Jackson has missed three games, counting the second half of Week 4. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Jackson was close to playing and is expected back in Week 8.

stories.text: Tyler Huntley throws for 298 yards in a losing effort
stories.summary: Huntley completed 23 of 34 passes for 298 yards with one touchdown and one interception against Cincinnati. The Bengals' Demetrius Knight Jr. made the pick. Baltimore scored 13 points all day and none in the second half.

stories.text: 35: unanswered points the Ravens allowed after halftime
stories.summary: Baltimore led 13-0 at the break and gave up 35 points in the second half. Per the Bengals, that makes Cincinnati the 10th team in NFL history to be blanked in the first half and still score 35 or more in the second.

stories.text: Ravens visit Bills on Sunday with Jackson likely back
stories.summary: Baltimore plays at Buffalo on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. Jackson is expected to return from the ankle sprain. Watch his mobility and whether the offense gets going before halftime.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals erase 13-0 deficit, rout Ravens

stories.text: Bengals score 35 second-half points to rout the Ravens
stories.summary: Cincinnati trailed 13-0 at halftime in Baltimore and won 35-13. It is the Bengals' first AFC North win of the year and moves them to 4-2. The defense allowed no second-half points and finished with four sacks.

stories.text: Tanner Hudson's torn pec and Swayze Bozeman's forearm
stories.summary: Backup tight end Tanner Hudson tore a pectoral muscle against Miami on Oct. 11, and his agent says he is expected to miss the rest of the season. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman broke his forearm in that game and went on injured reserve. Cincinnati signed linebacker Jack Kiser. These are the most recent details found, from Oct. 13.

stories.text: Tee Higgins hauls in 148 yards and a score at Baltimore
stories.summary: Higgins caught 6 passes for 148 yards and a 13-yard touchdown. He now has 6,012 career receiving yards in 91 games. Ja'Marr Chase added 5 catches for 62 yards and a touchdown.

stories.text: 16-for-18: Joe Burrow's second half in Baltimore
stories.summary: Burrow went 16 of 18 for 249 yards and all four of his touchdown passes after halftime. He finished 22 of 30 for 292 yards. He is the only quarterback this season with four touchdown passes in a single half.

stories.text: Bengals host the Titans in Week 8
stories.summary: Cincinnati plays Tennessee at Paycor Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. The Bengals' pass rush has at least two sacks in every game this season and has 21 in total.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Szmyt's late kick lifts Browns past Titans

stories.text: Browns beat Tennessee 27-24 on a last-second field goal
stories.summary: Andre Szmyt kicked a 31-yard field goal as time expired to give Cleveland its fifth win in six games and a 5-2 record. Deshaun Watson ran in the go-ahead touchdown with 4:34 left, then Cam Ward tied it for Tennessee with 58 seconds to play. Watson answered with a four-play, 55-yard drive.

stories.text: Tytus Howard in concussion evaluation after leaving early
stories.summary: Right tackle Tytus Howard left in the third quarter to be checked for a concussion. Nickel corner Myles Harden (hamstring) and defensive tackle Mason Graham (knee) also exited but came back in the fourth quarter. Running back Quinshon Judkins returned after missing one game.

stories.text: KC Concepcion posts his first 100-yard receiving game
stories.summary: Concepcion went over 100 receiving yards for the first time and finished with 152 scrimmage yards. He also dropped a 48-yard touchdown pass from Watson. Watson finished with 327 total yards.

stories.text: 14-0: the early hole the Browns climbed out of
stories.summary: Tennessee led 14-0 after Tony Pollard ran for 61 yards and a score on the opening drive, and Cleveland committed two first-half turnovers. Judkins ran for 96 yards and two first-half touchdowns, and the Browns stopped Pollard on fourth-and-goal from the 1 to keep it from getting worse.

stories.text: Browns visit the Steelers in a 5-2 AFC North showdown
stories.summary: Cleveland plays at Pittsburgh on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. The Steelers ran for 148 yards against New Orleans, so the Browns' run defense gets a test.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers grind out win over Saints in Paris

stories.text: Steelers run past the Saints 16-10 in Paris
stories.summary: Pittsburgh ran for 148 yards to New Orleans' 18 and converted 10 of 16 third downs. The win moves the Steelers to 5-2. Payton Wilson intercepted Tyler Shough in the red zone to stop a New Orleans drive.

stories.text: Watt, Dowdle and Highsmith carried designations into Paris
stories.summary: Per the team's Week 7 report, T.J. Watt (calf) and Alex Highsmith (groin) were both practicing before the trip, and neither carried a game designation. Watt had a sack against New Orleans. Rico Dowdle (knee) was questionable and played, finishing with 86 scrimmage yards. Receiver Ben Skowronek and cornerback Brandin Echols were ruled out. This is the pregame report. No postgame update was found.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren runs for 101 yards and adds 36 receiving
stories.summary: Warren led the Steelers' ground game with 101 rushing yards and 36 more through the air. Dowdle added 41 rushing yards and 45 receiving. Linebacker Patrick Queen had a team-high 10 tackles and a sack on New Orleans' last offensive play.

stories.text: 540: Aaron Rodgers' career touchdown passes
stories.summary: Rodgers threw his 540th career touchdown pass, to Darnell Washington on a 77-yard, six-play drive. That moved him past Peyton Manning into third on the all-time list.

stories.text: Browns come to Pittsburgh before the Steelers' bye
stories.summary: Pittsburgh hosts Cleveland on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS. A win would put the Steelers at 6-2 heading into their Week 9 bye. Cleveland has won five of its last six.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans fall in OT, still winless at home

stories.text: Texans drop overtime game to Giants, fall to 0-4 at home
stories.summary: Houston lost 27-21 in overtime on Sunday and sits at 2-5. C.J. Stroud hit Xavier Hutchinson for a 3-yard touchdown with 52 seconds left to force overtime, but the Texans went three-and-out on their extra-period drive. New York then covered 81 yards in three plays, capped by Devin Singletary's 30-yard touchdown run.

stories.text: Jaylin Noel leaves in a boot with turf toe
stories.summary: Receiver Jaylin Noel hurt his toe on a fourth-quarter kickoff return and did not come back. Coach DeMeco Ryans said Noel has turf toe and he left the stadium in a boot. His timeline is unclear, but Houston has its bye next week to buy him time.

stories.text: Marvin Harrison Jr. finds the end zone in his second game as a Texan
stories.summary: Harrison caught a 6-yard touchdown from Stroud with about 30 seconds left in the second quarter, and Cade Stover's two-point catch tied the game at 14. It was Harrison's second game with Houston since the trade from Arizona. Tank Dell also played his first game back after nearly two years away with a knee injury, with one catch for 43 yards.

stories.text: 153: C.J. Stroud's passing yards, a season low
stories.summary: Stroud went 17 of 28 for 153 yards and two touchdowns against New York. Houston was outgained by 183 yards in the game. The Texans are 0-4 at home this season.

stories.text: Bye week, then a trip to Los Angeles to face the Chargers
stories.summary: Houston is off in Week 8. The Texans return Nov. 8 at the Chargers, with kickoff at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch how many of the injured receivers are back after the break.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts lose third straight, stick with Jones

stories.text: Colts fall to unbeaten Vikings 16-10 for a third straight loss
stories.summary: Indianapolis led most of the way after Jonathan Taylor's 38-yard touchdown run on the opening drive, then went quiet. Spencer Shrader missed two second-half field goals, including a 56-yarder on fourth-and-2, and Harrison Smith intercepted Daniel Jones near midfield with about a minute left. Coach Shane Steichen said he has a ton of faith in Jones and is not considering a change at quarterback.

stories.text: Secondary thinned out as Gardner sits and two starters leave
stories.summary: Cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) was inactive. Justin Walley (knee) and Cam Taylor-Britt (groin) both left the game with injuries. Tight end Tyler Warren (groin) missed his second straight game, while Jaylon Carlies (ribs) returned after two games out.

stories.text: Spencer Shrader's perfect run ends, but he still leads the league in scoring
stories.summary: Shrader's streak of 22 straight made field goals ended with a wide-left miss against Minnesota. He still leads the NFL with 70 points. Grover Stewart also blocked a 59-yard attempt by Vikings kicker Will Reichard in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: 108: Daniel Jones' passing yards against Minnesota
stories.summary: Jones went 13 of 22 and absorbed four sacks that cost 44 yards. Through seven games he has four touchdown passes and seven interceptions. Minnesota's defense has allowed a league-low 74 points.

stories.text: Colts head to Jacksonville to face the Jaguars
stories.summary: Indianapolis visits Jacksonville on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Jaguars (4-2) are coming off their bye. Watch whether the Colts can protect Jones against a rested front.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars at 4-2 at the bye, Harrison out for year

stories.text: Jaguars hit the bye at 4-2 and need a left tackle
stories.summary: Anton Harrison tore his ACL, which surgeons found during knee surgery, so his season is over. Walker Little and Cole Van Lanen are the healthy tackles on the roster. Jacksonville has about $3.66 million in cap space, 30th in the league, so help before the Nov. 10 trade deadline will be hard to add.

stories.text: Four Jaguars on injured reserve, Montaric Brown unsettled
stories.summary: Harrison, safety Caleb Ransaw (knee), lineman Patrick Mekari (back) and edge rusher BJ Green II (upper body) are all on injured reserve. Coach Liam Coen called Mekari the closest to returning, with Green second. Cornerback Montaric Brown, who has a hamstring injury from Week 3, is not on IR and his status was due after the bye.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence is off to the best start of his career
stories.summary: Lawrence has 14 touchdown passes and four interceptions while completing better than 65 percent of his throws. He was pulled early from two games because the result was already decided.

stories.text: 3.5: sacks combined from Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen
stories.summary: The two edge rushers have only 3.5 sacks between them through six games, and the pass rush is the top need the report card flags. Jacksonville could look for a defensive tackle or rusher before the deadline.

stories.text: Jaguars host the Colts after the bye
stories.summary: Jacksonville was off in Week 7. The Jaguars host Indianapolis on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS, then play at Baltimore on Thursday, Nov. 5 on Prime Video. Watch the left tackle spot against a Colts team that gave up four sacks on Sunday.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans lose on last play, stall at the goal line

stories.text: Titans lose 27-24 to Browns on a last-play field goal
stories.summary: Tennessee led 14-7 in the second quarter and had first-and-goal at the Cleveland 4, but came away with no points after four plays. Tony Pollard's apparent touchdown was overturned on review. Cleveland then drove for Andre Szmyt's 32-yard field goal as time expired, a loss that cost the Titans a chance at back-to-back wins for the first time since 2022.

stories.text: Spears, Ridley and three others were questionable going in
stories.summary: Tyjae Spears (knee), Calvin Ridley (hip), Kevin Winston Jr. (quad), Tony Adams (ankle) and Dorian Mausi (foot) all carried a questionable tag on the Friday report. A postgame column said Spears was unhealthy again, which left Pollard as the lead back. This is the last official report available, so check Wednesday's practice sheet for updates.

stories.text: Tony Pollard runs for 129 yards and three touchdowns
stories.summary: Pollard carried 25 times for 129 yards and scored from 36, 10 and 1 yards out. His last score tied the game with 58 seconds left. He had 77 yards and two touchdowns on his first eight carries.

stories.text: 491: yards the Browns gained on the Titans defense
stories.summary: Cleveland piled up 491 yards and 26 first downs. Deshaun Watson threw for 308 yards, and Quinshon Judkins ran for 96 yards and two scores. Coach Robert Saleh called it just not a good enough day on defense.

stories.text: Titans travel to Cincinnati to face the Bengals
stories.summary: Tennessee plays at Cincinnati on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Rookie receiver Carnell Tate had 344 yards through six games, a Titans-era rookie record. Cam Ward went 20 of 31 for 181 yards against Cleveland.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos win third straight, Chiefs next

stories.text: Broncos beat Cardinals 30-16 for a third straight win
stories.summary: Denver led by 17 in the fourth quarter and matched its season high with 30 points. The 14-point margin is the largest of the year. Five different players had a play of 20 yards or more, and Arizona went 1 of 5 in the red zone.

stories.text: Waddle leaves with a chest injury before the Chiefs game
stories.summary: Jaylen Waddle went to the medical tent in the fourth quarter after a reverse broke down and did not return. He had been limited in practice with a chest issue. Sean Payton gave no update and called the play "awful." Pat Surtain II missed a third straight game with an ankle injury, but he was limited in practice and there is optimism he plays Sunday. Zach Allen hurt a hamstring late.

stories.text: Bo Nix runs 62 yards for the longest QB touchdown in team history
stories.summary: Nix broke loose for a 62-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, the longest by a Denver quarterback. He also threw a 52-yard screen touchdown to RJ Harvey, which makes him the fifth quarterback in NFL history with a 50-yard passing score and a 50-yard rushing score in one game. He finished with 73 rushing yards.

stories.text: 19: Alex Singleton's tackles against Arizona
stories.summary: Singleton piled up 19 tackles, plus a sack, a tackle for loss and two quarterback hits. Malcolm Roach also had a sack and now has 2.5 on the season. Wil Lutz hit all three field goals and made his 111th straight extra point.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Denver Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City beat Denver 31-10 in Week 1 but comes in off its first loss of the season. Denver is 5-2. Watch whether Surtain returns to the secondary and whether Waddle is on the injury report. Trey McBride caught 10 passes against the Broncos without Surtain and Talanoa Hufanga.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Seahawks end Chiefs' unbeaten start 20-3

stories.text: Seahawks hand the Chiefs their first loss, 20-3
stories.summary: Seattle held Kansas City to 213 yards and 11 first downs on Sunday night. The Chiefs went 3 of 11 on third down and never reached the red zone. Patrick Mahomes was 19 of 33 for 165 yards with an interception. Harrison Butker missed field goals from 58 and 45 yards.

stories.text: Bolton shakes off neck spasms, Moore nears return
stories.summary: Andy Reid said linebacker Nick Bolton had neck spasms, missed one snap and should work through it. Right tackle Jaylon Moore sat out in concussion protocol and may clear it this week, which would help after Joshua Ezeudu struggled in his first start. Rashee Rice is several weeks past a hamstring injury and could return to practice in some form next Wednesday.

stories.text: Kelce moves into fifth on the career receptions list
stories.summary: Travis Kelce caught four passes for 44 yards in the loss and passed into fifth place on the NFL's all-time receptions list. He was one of the few Chiefs to find room against a Seattle defense that gave up no red-zone trips.

stories.text: 0: Red-zone trips for the Chiefs in Seattle
stories.summary: Kansas City never got inside the 20 on 213 total yards. Seattle, by comparison, went 11 of 16 on third down and piled up 410 yards. The Chiefs' kicking trouble came on long tries: Butker missed from 58 and from 45.

stories.text: Chiefs at Broncos Sunday, 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City (5-1) visits Denver (5-2) in a division game with the AFC West lead in play. The Chiefs won the Week 1 meeting 31-10. Watch the right tackle spot, where Moore's return would settle the line, and whether the offense reaches the red zone against a defense that held Arizona to one touchdown in five trips.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders drop fourth straight to the Rams

stories.text: Rams run past Raiders 35-21, Las Vegas loses a fourth straight
stories.summary: Los Angeles led 28-6 at halftime and the Raiders never got closer than two scores. They scored twice in the fourth quarter but failed both two-point tries and missed on fourth down in Rams territory. Las Vegas is 3-4.

stories.text: Patrick Johnson leaves with a neck stinger
stories.summary: Patrick Johnson did not return from Sunday's loss after a stinger in his neck. He had a similar stinger in Week 5 against the Patriots. The Raiders have not given a designation for Week 8 yet.

stories.text: Cousins throws for 295 yards and two scores in the loss
stories.summary: Kirk Cousins threw touchdowns to Tre Tucker and Ashton Jeanty and leads the NFL with 16 touchdown passes. Tucker had five catches for 103 yards. Jeanty caught eight passes for 61 yards but the running game managed only 42 yards on 14 carries.

stories.text: 3 of 14: Raiders' third-down conversions against the Rams
stories.summary: Los Angeles held Las Vegas to three conversions on 14 third-down tries and stopped the offense on fourth down. The Rams rushed for nearly 200 yards, led by Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, and kept the Raiders' offense off the field.

stories.text: Raiders at Jets Sunday, 1:00 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Las Vegas (3-4) travels to face the Jets, who are 2-5. The Raiders need to stop a four-game skid. Watch whether they can settle the offensive line and convert third downs, the weak spot against the Rams.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers weigh offensive changes

stories.text: Harbaugh will not rule out moving Mike McDaniel off play-calling
stories.summary: Jim Harbaugh said the staff is "looking into everything" at 0-6 and that the process is ongoing. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk reported Adam Gase could replace McDaniel, and the team may reassign him. The Athletic reported the offense will try to simplify in the coming weeks. The Chargers are on their bye.

stories.text: Bye week, no named designations after a banged-up line
stories.summary: The Chargers have no game this week and no confirmed injury designations. Their offensive line has been hit by injuries all season, and it has allowed 21 sacks through six games. The team will release its first practice report ahead of the Rams game.

stories.text: Justin Herbert is last among qualified QBs in adjusted QBR
stories.summary: Herbert has eight interceptions and a league-worst 10 turnovers through six games. His adjusted QBR of 29.9 ranks last among qualified quarterbacks and his 68.8 passer rating is 31st of 33. He is completing 59.4 percent of his passes behind a line that has allowed 21 sacks.

stories.text: 15: Points per game for the Chargers, 30th in the NFL
stories.summary: Los Angeles averages 15.0 points and 287.2 yards per game, 26th in yards. The offense scored no touchdowns in the 22-6 loss to Kansas City. The defense is the bright spot: eighth in success rate with 10 takeaways, tied for third in the league.

stories.text: Chargers host the Rams Sunday, 4:05 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: After the bye, Los Angeles hosts the Rams at SoFi Stadium on Nov. 1. Watch who calls the plays, since Harbaugh has not ruled out a change. The Chargers also get a second look at a Rams run game that just put up nearly 200 yards in Las Vegas.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Prescott's turnovers cloud Monday night trip

stories.text: Prescott's interceptions have stalled the Cowboys offense
stories.summary: Dak Prescott threw four interceptions in the last two games, and Dallas scored 29 points total in losses to Tampa Bay and Green Bay. The Cowboys arrive in Philadelphia at 2-4, and Brian Schottenheimer still answers questions about game management.

stories.text: Turpin, Shelton and Winters out against Philadelphia
stories.summary: Receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs), tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring) and linebacker Dee Winters are ruled out. Linebacker Marist Liufau and safety P.J. Locke are questionable and must come off injured reserve to play. Cornerback Cobie Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown practiced fully Saturday with no designation.

stories.text: Rashan Gary piles up nine pressures in the Green Bay loss
stories.summary: Gary tied his career high with nine pressures against the Packers. He is the only Cowboys pass rusher with more than five pressures in a game this season. Kenny Clark added his first sack of the year.

stories.text: 21: times Green Bay pressured Prescott
stories.summary: Prescott went 11 of 19 for 74 yards and a touchdown when pressured against the Packers. The Cowboys also ran only 15 times for 48 yards while throwing 54 passes, a split Schottenheimer said was not the plan.

stories.text: At Philadelphia tonight, then Arizona at home
stories.summary: Dallas visits the Eagles tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Watch whether the Cowboys protect Prescott against an Eagles team starting Tanner McKee at quarterback. Arizona visits next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: McCarthy wins first start, Giants lead the East

stories.text: McCarthy wins his first start as Giants beat Texans in overtime
stories.summary: J.J. McCarthy went 20 of 28 for 252 yards in the 27-21 win in Houston, and Devin Singletary ran 30 yards for the winner in overtime. The Giants lead the NFC East at 4-2-1 heading into their bye.

stories.text: Edmunds goes to injured reserve, two defensive backs miss out
stories.summary: Linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) was placed on injured reserve. Safety Jevon Holland and cornerback Greg Newsome II sat out with concussions. Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. left with a hamstring injury late in the second quarter. Tyler Nubin, Paulson Adebo and Jermaine Eluemunor returned.

stories.text: Cam Skattebo runs for a career high 124 yards
stories.summary: Skattebo carried 17 times after playing only six snaps the week before. He scored from 16 yards to put New York ahead 21-14, then broke a 42-yard run in overtime to set up the winning score.

stories.text: 4: rushing touchdowns, a first for the Giants since 1950
stories.summary: New York scored four times on the ground against Houston and held the Texans to 84 rushing yards. Malik Nabers also posted his fourth straight 100-yard receiving game.

stories.text: Bye in Week 8, then at Philadelphia
stories.summary: The Giants are off this week as NFC East leaders. They play at Philadelphia on Sunday, Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. Watch how quickly the injured defensive backs return.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles try to stop a four game skid without Hurts

stories.text: Eagles play on without Hurts and chase the division
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee makes his fourth career start tonight against Dallas. Philadelphia has lost four straight at 2-4 and still sits one game behind the 4-2-1 Giants.

stories.text: DeVonta Smith out, Barkley questionable with a hamstring
stories.summary: Receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), defensive back Michael Carter II, edge rusher Nolan Smith and receiver Dontayvion Wicks are out. Saquon Barkley is questionable but practiced fully Saturday. Tight end Dallas Goedert is cleared. Several players on injured reserve need activation by Monday afternoon to play.

stories.text: Tanner McKee gets another start behind a patched line
stories.summary: McKee went 26 of 45 for 215 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in the loss to Carolina. He plays behind a line that lost Lane Johnson to retirement and traded away Cam Jurgens.

stories.text: 5.0: second half points per game, last in the league
stories.summary: The Eagles also rank last in first downs and total yards in the second half and have scored 24 or fewer points in nine straight games. First time play-caller Sean Mannion is under the microscope.

stories.text: Dallas tonight, then Washington on Sunday night
stories.summary: Philadelphia hosts the Cowboys tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Next Sunday, Nov. 1, the Eagles visit Washington at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. Watch how Mannion's offense moves in the second half.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders regroup after bye, McLaurin lost for year

stories.text: Quinn keeps his job and the staff adds Steve Wilks
stories.summary: Washington is 1-4-1 and last in the NFC East. NFL Network reporters say Dan Quinn bought time with the effort in San Francisco, though wins still have to come. The team hired Steve Wilks to help with defensive game planning.

stories.text: McLaurin done for the season, Croskey-Merritt on IR
stories.summary: Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon in the first quarter against the 49ers and will miss the rest of the year. Running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve for at least four weeks. Laremy Tunsil has been out, and center has stayed unsettled.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels posts a season best passer rating
stories.summary: Daniels went 29 of 40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions against San Francisco, a 110.4 rating. He has five touchdown passes and no interceptions this season. He wears a brace on his left arm.

stories.text: 0-3-1: Washington's record in Daniels's starts
stories.summary: Daniels has started four of six games, and the Commanders have not won one of them. Their lone win came in Week 3 with Marcus Mariota at quarterback.

stories.text: Off this week, then Philadelphia on Sunday night
stories.summary: Washington is on its bye. The Commanders host the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC, then face the Rams. Watch how the receivers fill in for McLaurin.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Williams outduels Maye in prime time

stories.text: Bears hold off Patriots 30-24 on Thursday night
stories.summary: Caleb Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns at Soldier Field, and Cairo Santos kicked a 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left to seal it. The Bears moved to 5-2 and beat Drake Maye and New England after a short week. D'Marco Jackson's end zone interception of Maye in the second quarter set up a Chicago touchdown.

stories.text: Kmet and Muhammad leave Patriots game hurt
stories.summary: Cornerback Malik Muhammad left in the third quarter with a toe injury. Tight end Cole Kmet hurt his right knee on a catch with 5:34 left. Watch the practice reports this week, because Chicago turns around for a Monday night trip to Seattle.

stories.text: Burden goes for 130 yards and a score
stories.summary: Luther Burden caught four passes for 130 yards, including a 24-yard touchdown, against New England. Colston Loveland added a 12-yard touchdown catch as Williams spread the ball around.

stories.text: 308: Williams makes Bears history again
stories.summary: Williams is the first Bears quarterback with 300 passing yards in back-to-back games since Mitch Trubisky in 2018. He threw for 305 against Atlanta the week before, in his first game back from a hamstring injury, and added 308 with two touchdowns and no interceptions against New England.

stories.text: At Seattle on Monday night, Nov. 2
stories.summary: The Bears travel to face the Seahawks on Monday, Nov. 2 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Watch whether Williams can keep the passing pace on another short turnaround, and how Kmet and Muhammad hold up.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Bates wins it as time expires vs. Packers

stories.text: Bates kicks Lions past Packers 20-17 at the gun
stories.summary: Jake Bates hit a 22-yard field goal as time expired to beat Green Bay at Ford Field. Detroit won back-to-back games for the first time since early October 2025 and moved to 4-2. Brian Branch intercepted Jordan Love in the fourth quarter in his first game back from an Achilles injury.

stories.text: Rakestraw hurt his ankle, Mays back at center
stories.summary: Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. left in the second half with an ankle injury and did not return. Center Cade Mays came off injured reserve and started his first game of the season. Branch also played after his Achilles recovery.

stories.text: St. Brown piles up 153 yards on nine catches
stories.summary: Amon-Ra St. Brown caught nine passes for 153 yards against Green Bay. Jared Goff finished 22 of 32 for 303 yards and two touchdowns, and Jameson Williams caught two of them.

stories.text: 60: Lions hold Green Bay to 60 rushing yards
stories.summary: Detroit gave up 60 yards on the ground and no rushing touchdowns to the Packers. On the other side, Jahmyr Gibbs carried 29 times for 116 yards and added five catches for 27 yards.

stories.text: Vikings come to Ford Field on Sunday, Nov. 1
stories.summary: Detroit hosts unbeaten Minnesota (6-0) on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Lions will need to slow a Vikings defense that held Indianapolis to 44 total yards, and they will check on Rakestraw's ankle first.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Kicking misses cost Packers in Detroit

stories.text: Packers drop 20-17 decision in Detroit
stories.summary: Green Bay's three-game win streak ended on Bates's walk-off field goal. Rookie kicker Trey Smack missed two field goals, and the Packers' streak of 10 straight fourth-down conversions ended when D.J. Reed stopped Matthew Golden on fourth-and-4. Love said afterward the offense did not meet its standard.

stories.text: Rhyan, Monk and Wyatt all hurt against Lions
stories.summary: Center Sean Rhyan left with an ankle injury and was ruled out at the start of the third quarter. Backup center Jacob Monk went down with a quad injury, and John Williams replaced him. Defensive tackle Devonte Wyatt headed to the locker room with an ankle injury before halftime. Green Bay plays again Thursday, so the status of all three matters fast.

stories.text: Jacobs scores in his season debut
stories.summary: Josh Jacobs returned from injury and caught five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown, breaking two tackles on a 25-yard score. He added 36 yards on 11 carries. He also dropped a possible touchdown on a third-down route late.

stories.text: 17: Packers' second-lowest point total this year
stories.summary: Green Bay's 17 points tied for the second-fewest it has scored this season. Love went 27 of 45 for 274 yards with two touchdowns and an interception, and the offense stalled on late drives.

stories.text: Panthers visit Lambeau on Thursday, Oct. 29
stories.summary: Green Bay hosts Carolina on Thursday, Oct. 29 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. With the offensive line and defensive line banged up, watch who starts at center on a short week.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings stay perfect with 16-10 win

stories.text: Vikings beat Colts 16-10 to reach 6-0
stories.summary: Minnesota reached its best start since 2009 at U.S. Bank Stadium. Kyler Murray ran for 35 yards and threw a fourth-quarter touchdown to T.J. Hockenson, and the defense shut Indianapolis out in the second half.

stories.text: Mason was the lone Viking with a game designation
stories.summary: Before Sunday's game, running back Jordan Mason was listed questionable after being designated to return from injured reserve, and coach Kevin O'Connell said he expected him to be available. Justin Jefferson (ankle), Brian O'Neill (knee) and James Pierre (foot) went full in practice on Thursday and Friday after limited Wednesdays. This is the final pregame report, so check this week's practice reports for post-game changes.

stories.text: Cashman collects two sacks and nine tackles
stories.summary: Linebacker Blake Cashman had two sacks and nine tackles in the win over Indianapolis. He led a defense that sacked the Colts four times and pressured Daniel Jones all afternoon.

stories.text: 44: total yards the Colts managed
stories.summary: Brian Flores's defense held Indianapolis to 44 total yards and four sacks. Kicker Will Reichard also passed Gary Anderson's franchise record of 35 straight made field goals, though a 59-yard try was later blocked.

stories.text: At Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1 against the Lions
stories.summary: Minnesota visits the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 1 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Lions just beat Green Bay on a last-second kick, so expect a tight division game. Watch whether Jefferson and Mason are healthy.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons end the 49ers' unbeaten run

stories.text: Falcons end San Francisco's unbeaten start, 29-20
stories.summary: Atlanta trailed 14-3, then scored on four straight possessions and won its first game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium this season. Michael Penix Jr. threw a touchdown to Kyle Pitts to open the second half and another to Drake London in the fourth quarter. Kendal Daniels picked off Brock Purdy late to seal it.

stories.text: Robinson, Deablo and Bowman sit out; London clears concussion check
stories.summary: Running back Brian Robinson Jr. missed the game with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Divine Deablo and safety Billy Bowman Jr. were also out. Drake London was evaluated for a concussion in the third quarter, passed the check and returned. Cornerbacks A.J. Terrell and C.J. Henderson were back on the field.

stories.text: Drake London: 7 catches, 66 yards and a touchdown
stories.summary: London caught seven of his 10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown against San Francisco. He scored in the fourth quarter to push the lead to 25-14. Penix leaned on him on third downs all afternoon.

stories.text: 6 of 35: dropbacks on which Penix was pressured
stories.summary: San Francisco got to Michael Penix Jr. on just 17.1 percent of his dropbacks, and he took no sacks. He threw three touchdown passes without an interception. The 49ers outgained Atlanta 400 to 295 and still lost, because the Falcons forced four turnovers.

stories.text: At Tampa Bay, Sunday, Nov. 1, 1:00 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Atlanta visits the Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium for its first NFC South game of the year. A win would put the Falcons at 4-4. Tampa Bay ran for 258 yards against Carolina, so the Atlanta run defense gets a test.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers lose Moton after 43-13 rout

stories.text: Panthers get run over by Tampa Bay, 43-13
stories.summary: Carolina allowed 258 rushing yards and committed three turnovers in the loss at home. The Bucs led 33-6 at halftime and the Panthers pulled their starters with 10:21 left. Carolina now has the league's worst run defense, and the schedule gives it a short week.

stories.text: Right tackle Taylor Moton has a fractured fibula
stories.summary: Moton went down late in the loss when players fell into his legs on a Bryce Young sack. Coach Dave Canales confirmed a fracture and did not rule out a lost season. Moton had just returned in Week 6 after missing four games with blood clots in his lungs. First-round pick Monroe Freeling took over at right tackle and is dealing with a knee injury himself.

stories.text: Bryce Young's 280-yard streak ends at five games
stories.summary: Young went 14 of 27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. The touchdown was a 50-yard throw to Darren Waller in the second quarter. He was sacked five times, and one strip-sack was returned for a Tampa Bay score. Both interceptions came from a clean pocket.

stories.text: 258: rushing yards the Panthers allowed to the Bucs
stories.summary: Tampa Bay ran 48 times and finished 25 yards short of its franchise single-game record. Bucky Irving had 106 and Kenneth Gainwell added 88. Carolina has given up about 227 rushing yards per game in its three losses.

stories.text: At Green Bay, Thursday, Oct. 29, 8:15 PM ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: The Panthers travel to Lambeau Field on a short week. They will need a plan at right tackle without Moton and a fix for a run defense that just gave up more than 250 yards.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints hit the bye at 2-5 under pressure

stories.text: Saints fall to Pittsburgh in Paris and head into the bye at 2-5
stories.summary: New Orleans lost 16-10 and now sits at 2-5 with the bye next. Owner Gayle Benson gave coach Kellen Moore and GM Mickey Loomis a public warning earlier this month, and the Saints scored 10 points on six drives against the Steelers. Four of those drives reached the Pittsburgh 35. Moore said the staff will evaluate everything during the bye.

stories.text: Safety Justin Reid leaves with a concussion
stories.summary: Reid was ruled out with a concussion just before halftime in Paris. Running back CJ Donaldson left in the first half with a shoulder injury. The bye gives both extra time before the Nov. 8 game against Cleveland.

stories.text: Tyler Shough: 30 of 38 for 278 yards
stories.summary: Shough threw a 1-yard touchdown to Devaughn Vele on fourth-and-goal to tie it at 10-10. His third-quarter pass for Chris Olave in the red zone was intercepted by Payton Wilson, and Shough took the blame afterward. Alvin Kamara caught seven passes for 57 yards and Olave had six for 56.

stories.text: 18: rushing yards on 17 carries against Pittsburgh
stories.summary: The Saints could not run the ball in Paris, and Moore said the run game needs work. Kamara and Kendre Miller combined for 11 yards on 14 carries. Kicker Daniel Carlson also missed a 52-yard field goal wide right in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Bye in Week 8, then Cleveland, Sunday, Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: New Orleans is off this weekend and returns home to the Caesars Superdome to face the Browns. Moore said the staff will look at everything during the break, including the kicking game, without committing to changes. A Week 10 home game against Carolina follows.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs rout Carolina with Mayfield back

stories.text: Bucs run over Carolina, 43-13, in Mayfield's return
stories.summary: Tampa Bay led 33-6 at halftime and won its first NFC South game of the year. Baker Mayfield returned from a dislocated right thumb and threw only 11 passes because the running game and defense did the work. The Bucs ran for 258 yards and forced four turnovers.

stories.text: Mayfield back from thumb; Gainwell has a brief hip scare
stories.summary: Mayfield played in a protective glove on his throwing hand after missing time with a dislocated thumb. Kenneth Gainwell left with a hip injury and returned. Before the game, receiver Emeka Egbuka, tackle Luke Goedeke and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. were ruled out with a concussion or foot issue, a calf injury and a rib injury.

stories.text: Bucky Irving: 106 yards and two touchdowns on 24 carries
stories.summary: Irving gained 73 of his yards after contact, a season high. Sean Tucker added a 46-yard touchdown run and Gainwell finished with 88 yards on 14 carries. The offensive line took much of the credit.

stories.text: 3: sacks for Yaya Diaby, after none in the first six games
stories.summary: Diaby finally broke through against Carolina, and Tampa Bay finished with five sacks. Al-Quadin Muhammad's strip-sack of Bryce Young was returned 32 yards for a touchdown by Calijah Kancey. The pressure rate on Young was 51.5 percent.

stories.text: Hosts Atlanta, Sunday, Nov. 1, 1:00 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Falcons come to Raymond James Stadium for Week 8. Tampa Bay is 1-0 in the division and has five more division games left. Atlanta beat undefeated San Francisco on Sunday, so this is no easy follow-up.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Red-zone trouble sinks Arizona again

stories.text: Cardinals fall 30-16 to Denver and stall in the red zone again
stories.summary: Arizona dropped to 2-5 at home against the Broncos. The offense failed to score a touchdown on most of its red-zone trips, and Jacoby Brissett took 13 quarterback hits behind a patched line. Coach Mike LaFleur called the final-drive play call at the goal line "a stupid call."

stories.text: Jeremiyah Love's status stays uncertain, safeties thin
stories.summary: Running back Jeremiyah Love sat out again, and Bam Knight carried the backfield load. Arizona was short at safety, so Garrett Williams played alongside Budda Baker. Brissett also played through a left hand injury, per NBC Sports. Love may return next week, but nothing is set.

stories.text: Trey McBride catches 10 for 111 and a score in a loss
stories.summary: The tight end led Arizona with 10 receptions, 111 yards and a touchdown against Denver. He crossed 400 career catches with 406. Two pass interference calls on him at the Denver 1 gave Arizona fresh downs on the last drive, but the Cardinals still came away empty.

stories.text: 13: quarterback hits Brissett took against Denver
stories.summary: Brissett went 27 of 48 for 272 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions, but he spent the afternoon under siege. The line started a seventh-round rookie at left tackle and a fourth-string right guard.

stories.text: At Dallas on Sunday, Nov. 1, 1:00 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Arizona travels to face the Cowboys in Week 8. Watch whether Love returns and whether the offense can finish drives in the red zone. The Cardinals then visit Seattle on Nov. 8.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams run past Raiders, Stafford sets mark

stories.text: Rams run over Las Vegas 35-21 to snap a two-game skid
stories.summary: Los Angeles led 28-6 at halftime and finished with 199 rushing yards. Sean McVay called the win "a good step in the right direction." The Rams host the winless Chargers next.

stories.text: McDuffie misses a second game, Nacua plays through calf
stories.summary: Cornerback Trent McDuffie sat out with a groin injury for the second straight game and could return soon. Puka Nacua was questionable with a calf injury but played and caught eight passes. Defensive lineman Kobie Turner is out at least three more games.

stories.text: Matthew Stafford becomes the Rams' all-time touchdown passer
stories.summary: Stafford threw three touchdown passes, two to Davis Allen and one to Puka Nacua, and passed Roman Gabriel's franchise mark. He now has 155 touchdown passes as a Ram. He finished 23 of 29 for 195 yards.

stories.text: 199: rushing yards for the Rams in Las Vegas
stories.summary: Kyren Williams ran for 99 yards and a score and Blake Corum added 93 and a touchdown. More than half of the Rams' 386 yards came on the ground. Williams also lost a fumble.

stories.text: Home vs. Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 1, 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Los Angeles hosts a Chargers team that is still looking for its first win. Watch McDuffie's status and whether the run game keeps its pace. Road games at Washington and Arizona follow.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: Niners suffer first loss, head into bye

stories.text: 49ers fall 29-20 at Atlanta for their first loss
stories.summary: San Francisco outgained Atlanta 400 yards to 295 but gave the ball away four times. Brock Purdy threw two interceptions, and the Falcons scored 23 straight points after trailing 14-3. The 49ers now take their bye at 6-1.

stories.text: McCaffrey hurt his thigh but returned
stories.summary: Christian McCaffrey went to the locker room in the second quarter with a thigh injury, then came back and finished with 7 carries for 39 yards and a touchdown plus 6 catches for 61 yards. He said he will be fine. No official update came out, and the bye week gives him time.

stories.text: Rookie Kaelon Black runs for 60 at the half
stories.summary: The third-round pick from Indiana had 11 carries for 60 yards at halftime, including a 30-yard touchdown for his first NFL score. He also fumbled on a promising drive. Before Sunday he had 45 carries for 170 yards.

stories.text: 4: turnovers that undid a 400-yard day in Atlanta
stories.summary: San Francisco reached Atlanta territory on all nine drives and averaged 6.2 yards per play to the Falcons' 4.7. Purdy had two interceptions, and a Black fumble and a George Kittle fumble added to the damage.

stories.text: Bye in Week 8, then Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 8, 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: San Francisco is off this week. Watch how healthy McCaffrey and the receivers are when the team returns to host the Raiders at home.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks smother Chiefs behind JSN

stories.text: Seahawks beat Kansas City 20-3 and hand the Chiefs their first loss
stories.summary: Seattle gained 410 yards, converted 11 of 16 third downs and held Kansas City to 213 yards. The win snapped a two-game skid and moved Seattle within a game of San Francisco in the NFC West. Sunday night's victory came a few hours after the 49ers lost.

stories.text: Shaheed leaves with a knee injury
stories.summary: Receiver Rashid Shaheed was listed as questionable to return with a knee injury during the Chiefs game. The source does not say whether he came back, so watch this week's practice reports.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba posts 150 yards and a touchdown
stories.summary: He caught 9 passes for 150 yards, 129 of them in the first half, the most by a Seahawk in a half since Tyler Lockett in 2020. He leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and 8 receiving touchdowns, and has 100 yards in six of seven games.

stories.text: 36: straight games without allowing a 100-yard rusher
stories.summary: Seattle held Kansas City to 213 total yards and kept the Chiefs out of the red zone. Kenneth Walker III ran 14 times for 36 yards.

stories.text: Home vs. Chicago on Monday, Nov. 2, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: The Bears come in at 5-2. Seattle then hosts Arizona on Nov. 8.
